heroHeadline: PCG Says Drilling-Capable Chinese Survey Ship Spent 25 Days Unpermitted in Philippine EEZ, Three Weeks Inside Scarborough Shoal's Territorial Sea, as DFA Discloses 296 Diplomatic Protests Since 2022
heroSubtitle: Philippine Coast Guard spokesman Rear Admiral Jay Tarriela said September 4, 2026 that the Chinese marine geological survey vessel Haiyang Dizhi Shihao entered the Philippine exclusive economic zone near-midnight on August 10 and stayed until around September 1 — 25 days total, roughly three weeks of it inside the 12-nautical-mile territorial sea of Scarborough Shoal (Bajo de Masinloc) — without a Department of Foreign Affairs research permit. Tarriela said the 76-meter, drilling-capable vessel, operated by the Guangzhou Marine Geological Survey under China's Ministry of Natural Resources, disabled its AIS for stretches of the voyage, was tracked via Canada's Dark Vessel Detection program, and withdrew ahead of the ASEAN Summit. Two days earlier, on September 3, DFA Secretary Ma. Teresita Lazaro told a House budget hearing the Philippines has filed 296 diplomatic protests against China since 2022 — 39 of them in 2026 alone — while noting water-cannoning and laser incidents have 'sort of decreased' in frequency even as sovereignty intrusions like the survey vessel persist.
